account:
Something unusual seems to be being arranged, but I do not yet know its full purpose. Several townsfolk near the mill have repeated a report of a 'bridge or port change' discussed at the bakery, naming baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as present. None has given me a clear firsthand explanation. Neighbour explicitly denies knowing of such a proposal, so I should not treat the repeated report as established fact.

I personally heard neighbour ask for voluntary wheat or bread donations for a community supper, with freight receiving contributions. When questioned, neighbour said it is a neighbourly effort but claimed not to have confirmed its time or venue, leaving arrangements to unnamed organisers. A community meal is therefore a concrete activity worth following up, unlike the vague bridge rumour. Baker, freight and innkeeper could plausibly be involved in provisioning it, but that remains an inference.

My appointment records also contain an added eighteen-hundred great hall lighting inspection with builder, recorded as approved by me yesterday. Builder is now near the mill. Neighbour has agreed to accompany me to that inspection after our usual fifteen-hundred tea, although I have office duties at sixteen-thirty. The inspection, escort and supper might be connected—perhaps preparations for a gathering—but I have no confirmation and cannot yet say it is intended for me or being concealed from me.

I have attended the mill for the ten-hundred grain inspection, but nobody has yet supplied a useful account of stocks or deliveries. I still need to keep lunch at home at noon, office at thirteen, tea at the dockside cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the hall inspection at eighteen. I should seek concrete details from those organising or supplying the supper rather than circulate an unsupported bridge rumour.
